coverageSpotVerification.detail: Full verification rather than a sample: the grader read all seven coverage manifests (evidence/coverage-m1..m6,m8.json) and all seven test modules (tests/m1..m6,m8.mjs) and traced every one of the 58 suite-required assertion->test mappings to the code that exercises the assertion's observable. Every mapping is honest and none is a stub: each mapped test asserts the assertion's actual observable (UI-rendered clauses go through Playwright against the exported web build, byte-level media clauses compare served bytes against the fixture, authorization clauses assert a specific server rejection). Two mappings were checked especially closely because they are the easiest to fake, and both hold: m3-a15's seed-idempotency mapping legitimately recurs in the M4/M5/M6/M8 manifests because the assertion text requires each milestone's suite to re-run it over every installed segment; and m6-a13 really replays the 50-action sample log and verifies resulting state rather than asserting on a stored receipt. The grader independently re-executed every sampled assertion and found no divergence between suiteResult and its own result. No milestone is adjudicated capability-failure.

defects.summary: chats:myChats silently truncates the conversation list to the 100 most recent (200 with the undocumented limit argument) with no cursor and no documentation, so an account above that many conversations can never enumerate the rest. The lane's own scale replay hit the underlying unbounded-read failure - logs/scale-replay.log records `Too many reads in a single function execution (limit: 4096)` thrown from dmCounterpart at convex/chats.ts:302 inside the myChats handler at line 384 - and the delivered fix is this cap (convex/chats.ts was rewritten at 19:33, minutes after the 19:30 crash). The grader confirmed the crash no longer reproduces: on the scale instance the 1000-conversation hub account u0001 now returns in 299 ms. But it returns only 100 rows, and 200 with limit:200, while u0500 (the named 100-conversation envelope fixture) fits exactly at the boundary. API.md documents neither the cap nor any way to page past it, and the web client calls myChats({}) with no limit and offers no load-more. Impact is bounded: messages are not lost and those conversations remain reachable by name through chats:dmByHandle / chats:groupByName and the /conversation/<handle> route - only list enumeration is truncated.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-01 (grading/work/probe-mychats.mjs against the scale instance; logs/scale-replay.log lines 78+; convex/chats.ts:296-427; src/components/ChatsPanel.tsx:17; API.md section 3)

defects.summary: Ordinary (non-view-once) media in a private conversation is served as an unauthenticated, non-expiring capability URL. A completely anonymous request to http://127.0.0.1:49301/api/storage/<uuid> for a photo sent inside a two-person DM returns HTTP 200 with the bytes; the URL carries no signature and no expiry, so anyone who obtains it keeps access for as long as the message exists. The lane handles the revocation cases the brief actually pins - delete revokes the asset (404) and view-once is a single-use no-store ticket that 410s on replay and after close, including from an unauthenticated context - so this is the unrevoked steady state only, and it is the stock Convex storage model rather than lane-authored logic. Recorded because 'authorization enforced server-side' reads more strictly than an unguessable-URL capability for private-chat media.

chats:markRead called by a user who is not a member of the chat returns success (null) instead of the `forbidden` ConvexError that every sibling function returns. It is a genuine no-op - convex/chats.ts:469 returns early when there is no active membership, so no state changes and no information leaks (the return value is null either way, so it is not an existence oracle) - but it is an inconsistent error surface against messages:list, messages:send, messages:react, chats:settings, search:inChat and chats:updateSettings, all of which correctly return forbidden for the same caller.

The scale-replay tool echoes a failing fixture action-log line verbatim into the lane's log, including the plaintext fixture password: logs/scale-replay.log line 78 reads `[REDACTED fixture action containing a password]`. This is the fixture pack's own committed credential rather than a user password, and the grader confirmed 0 plaintext-password occurrences across the dev and scale backend databases, the backend log and all 56 web/iOS bundle files - so m1-a13 still passes - but a replay diagnostic that prints credentials unredacted is the wrong default for a tool whose logs get published.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-04 (logs/scale-replay.log line 78, quoted redacted; grading/trace.md#m1-source for the full plaintext sweep)

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), placed well above 60 and held off 90 by the platform-proof clause.
O1.justification: 101 of the frozen manifest's 119 assertions pass under the grader's own execution: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18. M1-M5 are not merely solid but complete - every assertion independently re-executed through the custom-client API and Playwright against the exported web build, with no divergence from the suite. That is already past the 60 anchor, which presumes later milestones are patchy; here M6 and M8 are green on everything the web build can demonstrate (push seam with 80-char preview truncation and connected-client suppression, API.md sufficient for a grader-written variation on first attempt, 50-action adapter conformance with all 13 verbs, Insights, Trending, the scheduled digest including the restart and authorization cases). The 90 anchor is explicitly out of reach: it requires platform-proof artifacts, and all 9 native-artifact assertions (m6-a01..a07 cold-start offline reads, offline pending writes, ordered flush and receipts; m8-a17/a18 durable queue across app restart) were never demonstrated - the choreography receipts record ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as not-recorded. M7's 9 assertions are also not-passed in the denominator: this run's scope stops at M8 and M7 is a separate later session, but the frozen O1 rule keeps every in-scope milestone in the denominator regardless of status.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), nearer 90.
O2.justification: Beyond the checklist the grader found no blocker and no major defect: 2 minor (d-01 undocumented 100/200 conversation-list truncation with no cursor; d-02 unauthenticated non-expiring capability URLs for private-chat media) and 2 cosmetic (d-03 markRead returns success for a non-member instead of forbidden; d-04 a fixture credential echoed unredacted into a replay log). Adversarial probing of the core flows produced nothing: every outsider read and write against a private conversation is denied server-side with an explicit code (messages:list, messages:get, chats:settings, search:inChat, send, react, edit, remove, updateSettings all forbidden), anonymous callers are rejected on every surface including people search and upload-URL issuance, window enforcement is server-side and unspoofable because extra now/serverTimestamp arguments are rejected by the argument validator, pagination is capped at the documented 200 even when asked for 10000 against the 10k-message chat, input limits hold (post 500 chars, message 2000 chars, >4 images), view-once tickets are single-use and 410 on replay and after close including unauthenticated, delete revokes the asset, and a removed member sees pre-removal history only. It stays short of 90 because d-01 and d-02 are real behavioural gaps a user or third-party client could hit, not nits.

O4.anchorsCited: Against the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') and the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush'), both of which describe behaviour observed on a native proof; and the 90 anchor, which requires reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions and offline search all behaving as specced on the native proof, including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's artifacts, as the frozen prompt requires. There is no simulator artifact at all: both segment summaries record supplementalExternal ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as status 'not-recorded', pass null, and no m6-ios-screen.mp4, m6-ios-receipts.jsonl or run manifest exists anywhere in the lane. So nothing the anchors describe - cold-start offline history, previously-viewed media, cold-offline search, view-once not durably cached, two offline sends pending and flushing in order, receipts reaching read, the queue surviving app termination - was ever demonstrated on the platform the checklist names. That is the dominant fact and it holds the score below the 60 anchor, which presumes a native proof exists and shows reads working. It is not scored at or under 30 for two reasons the dimension explicitly credits. First, honesty of the gap between claim and guarantee is exemplary: the lane never asserts a native pass, the receipts carry the explicit not-recorded status with a reason, and the frozen harness spec itself sanctions the separation (greenRequired:false). Second, the rule names M8's multi-device convergence as additional O4 input and that evidence does exist and is mechanically checkable: m8-a15 records both warm-offline clients' writes settling in server-arrival order with no loss or duplicates (75.2/79.8 ms), m8-a16 records their receipts advancing normally, the M6 web segment records an ordered offline queue flush (181.5 ms), and m5-a12 records warm-offline search over synced messages - all schema-valid against the frozen receipts schema. The offline model the lane did demonstrate is clean; the native proof the dimension is really about is absent.

O5.bandRationale: First-match over the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. BAND 0 does not fire: the invariant manifest conforms - scale-verify-final.json records pass:true with all 18 per-entity counts exactly equal to invariant-manifest-combined.json (users 1008, posts 50228, messages 100015, conversations 1002, memberships 2053, quotedReplies 2736, activeReactions 2000, ...) and the named O5 fixtures exact, verified before the write probes ran; the grader re-checked the named fixtures directly against the running scale instance and found u0500 following 500 / 100 conversations, u0005 following 5, u0900 followers exactly 900, u0901's 5-account following list and g0001's 50-member roster all exact. The one named-fixture arithmetic difference, u0900 showing 246 posts against an expected 200, is fully accounted for by the 46 posts the lane's own celebrity write-path probes authored after verification (2 runs x (3 warm-ups + 20 samples)); it is a post-verification probe artifact, not a replay shortfall. Replay's wall cap was not exhausted: all 167,157 actions settled (receipt n=167157 settled:true) in 3,486 s of its own recorded clock; the rc=1 exit came from the post-replay inline verification, not the replay, and a standalone verification then passed. BAND 30 does not fire: the grader re-ran the probe set at the full corpus itself (sequential, 3 warm-ups, k=20, 30 s timeout) with no timeout, error or OOM, and every degradation rule passes with margin - deep paging page50/page1 p95 0.70x (limit 3x), 500-follow vs 5-follow feed 0.92x, celebrity-follower read path 1.38x, celebrity write path vs a 5-follower author 0.60x, busy-group send p95 14.4 ms so receipt aggregation across 50 members does not stall send, cold chat-list sync of the 100-conversation probe user 60.1 ms, and full-corpus values at or below the 10% checkpoint for global search (4.2 vs 3.0 ms), Insights (12.7 vs 12.8 ms) and Trending (63.0 vs 147.6 ms), all inside the 3x cross-checkpoint limit. The recorded 50% checkpoint readings sit above a straight line drawn between the 10% and full-corpus readings for those three metrics, which read literally would fire the mid-curve clause; the grader does not fire band 30 on them, because those probes ran at host load averages of 122-195 on an 18-core machine while the 10% and full-corpus probes ran at 16-25, and because the full-corpus endpoint is LOWER than the 50% reading on all three - a mid-curve value above the larger corpus cannot be corpus-driven growth, which is exactly what the rule's own parenthetical ('no superlinear blow-up mid-curve') scopes it to. BANDS 60 and 90 cannot fire on frozen inputs: both branches depend on absolute probe ceilings and a replay wall cap, and the frozen brief leaves both as P3 pilot-calibrated placeholders, so no ceiling utilisation and no cap fraction is computable - 90 in particular requires an affirmative '<=50% of ceiling' finding that no frozen ceiling supports. The function therefore falls through to 75: all rules and ceilings pass, 90's condition is not established.
